# taste-skill rules that fit the room

Pulled from taste-skill 2.5.1 (`references/system.md`, `layout-v4.md`, `copy.md`; MIT, see `LICENSE`) for the
room's own look. BRIEF §3 wins where they disagree (the riso inks, 2px borders, hard offset shadows).

## Type
- One display face plus one text face with fixed jobs, never three; at most four font files, loaded locally.
  (Room: Archivo Black display, IBM Plex Sans UI, IBM Plex Mono for her file and reasons.)
- Headlines carried by size and tight tracking (-0.5% to -4.5% at 40px and up), not by bold-and-big.
  Text weights 400 and 500 only.
- Each level at least 1.3x the next; body 16/26, small 14, labels 13 at 500. Nothing under 13px
  (stage mode: body 20px+). Lines at most 62 characters.
- Sentence case everywhere; never tracked capitals or small caps. Curly quotes; a number never breaks from its unit.
- Highlight by contrast, not by colour bars behind words. (Room exception, by the brief: the yellow highlighter
  sweep on "Sounds like", once.)
- Every word is live text, never baked into a picture.

## Colour
- The interface stays 90 to 95% neutral: paper and one near-black ink (never #000; the room's `#141414`).
  Hairlines and borders in that ink.
- One accent per surface: in the room, each seat's riso ink lives on its own card, glyph, sheet and tags only.
  Red stays for stamping.
- Contrast: reading text 7:1 on its ground, muted labels 4.5:1, large text 3:1. Yellow `#FFE800` always takes
  ink text.
- Never violet or lavender (hue ~270 to 330). No gradients, no scrims.

## Spacing and layout
- One spacing scale for every margin, gap and padding: 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128.
- Heading to content 48px (32 on a phone); cards 24px apart (12 on a phone).
- One radius family (room: 6px or less), one button shape, one card recipe, one link look. Two boxes deep at most.
- Equal left and right edges: everything on the same wrap lines or grid columns; no sideways scroll at 390.
- Tap targets 44px; one filled button marks the main action in any view.

## Motion
- Hover answers the pointer (a linked card lifts 2px, buttons step on hover and press on click); nothing tilts on
  hover (the room's landing tilt of 1-3° is a resting pose, not a hover).
- No fade-in on scroll, no parallax on text, no carousels or timed tabs. Under reduced motion everything rests.

## Copy
- Headings name things; buttons are a verb and an object ("Build the page"). No exclamation marks, no questions as
  headlines (the brief's one prompt, "What are we building today?", is the sheet's heading by design).
- No filler words (seamless, effortless, unlock, elevate, powerful, robust...), no slogans, no mood paragraphs.
